">AI-native technical support</a></li></ul></div></div></nav><div class="prose prose--block prose--blog col-span-full!"><p>Support investigations are fundamentally research problems, which is why the slowest part of responding to customer challenges has always been gathering the right context. By collapsing code, logs, team knowledge, and past conversations into a single Cursor session, we&#x27;ve removed that bottleneck for most of our work.</p>
<p>Today, over 75% of Cursor&#x27;s support interactions run through Cursor itself, increasing support engineer throughput 5–10x. This has led to a step-change in what is possible for support engineers from just a year ago.</p>
<h2 id="starting-from-the-codebase" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#starting-from-the-codebase" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Starting from the codebase</h2>
<p>When we investigate, we typically begin in Ask Mode. We point it at the symptom and let it trace backward through the relevant product behavior. Because our full codebase is available locally, Cursor can index and use semantic search across product code, docs, and internal tooling in the same session.</p>
<p>This is where multi-root workspaces become powerful. Product context almost always spans multiple repositories. Answering the user question, &quot;Why is this button disabled?&quot; might involve frontend logic, backend policy checks, and docs describing the expected behavior. We keep related repositories together in one workspace so that kind of question is answerable in a single thread.</p>
<h2 id="integrating-support-sources-with-mcp" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#integrating-support-sources-with-mcp" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Integrating support sources with MCP</h2>
<p>We use MCP servers to retrieve context and bring it into our investigations. Our support engineers no longer need to search across several tools to retrieve pertinent context because it is available in Cursor.</p>
<p>MCP servers allow us to integrate:</p>
<ul>
<li>Databases with customer information, such as subscription tier, team settings, and privacy settings</li>
<li>Streamed event logs containing details on services used, telemetry errors, and network issues</li>
<li>Communication platforms like Slack, filled with threads and conversations that fill out our understanding of how customers interact with the product.</li>
<li>Engineering ticket platforms containing potentially dozens of unique teams that each operate differently</li>
<li>An internal documentation service that contains run books and troubleshooting guides</li>
<li>An account management service containing crucial customer information that may change the tone of how you approach a customer</li>
</ul>
<p>With Cursor and MCP servers, our support engineers can quickly pull necessary information directly into their codebase investigations.</p>
<h3 id="identifying-where-the-failure-occurred" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#identifying-where-the-failure-occurred" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Identifying where the failure occurred</h3>
<p>When a customer reports an error, we need to understand: Is the problem they&#x27;re experiencing reproducible or transient, and where exactly did Cursor fail (client-side, API edge, downstream dependency, auth). Datadog MCP lets us pull the relevant logs and traces directly into the investigation thread, allowing us to start narrowing down the possibilities.</p>
<h3 id="tracking-down-similar-cases" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#tracking-down-similar-cases" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Tracking down similar cases</h3>
<p>When a new support ticket comes in, the issue has likely been seen by another customer or someone on our team. An MCP that integrates with your support platform, as well as Slack, allows us to search that context directly and bring the most relevant threads back into the investigation. We search for hard identifiers first (error strings, request IDs), broaden if needed, and look for the newest thread that includes a current status, a workaround, and an owner.</p>
<h3 id="determining-whether-it-was-a-bug" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#determining-whether-it-was-a-bug" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Determining whether it was a bug</h3>
<p>A lot of investigations come down to &quot;bug or expected behavior?&quot; Notion MCP lets us pull the relevant runbook into the thread, cross-reference it against what we&#x27;re seeing, and either confirm the behavior or escalate with a much clearer bug report.</p>
<h3 id="filing-a-bug-report" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#filing-a-bug-report" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Filing a bug report</h3>
<p>By the time we finish an investigation in Cursor, we&#x27;ve gathered all the material we need to file a ticket with engineering if something needs to be fixed. The Linear MCP lets us take all of that context and turn it into a formatted escalation directly from the same thread.</p>
<h3 id="documentation-updates" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#documentation-updates" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Documentation updates</h3>
<p>When multiple customers run into the same questions, it&#x27;s often a sign that we need to improve our documentation. Technical support is well-positioned to implement these kinds of fixes directly. We just mention @Cursor in Slack with what needs updating, and a cloud agent will open a PR against our docs repo.</p>
<h2 id="automating-the-process" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#automating-the-process" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Automating the process</h2>
<h3 id="commands-for-common-steps" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#commands-for-common-steps" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Commands for common steps</h3>
<p>We use slash commands for the most frequently repeated steps in the process:</p>
<div class="text-theme-text w-full " data-slot="accordion-root" data-orientation="vertical"><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_15fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_5fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Create Support Ticket<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_15fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_5fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Create Support Ticket
Create a Linear ticket for the reported bug or user issue.

## Format
- **Reporter Information:** Email, account ID, platform, app version
- **Summary:** Brief 1-2 sentence description
- **Expected vs Actual:** What should happen vs what happens
- **Steps to Reproduce:** Numbered list

## Notes
- Gather user info from logs before creating the ticket
- Include request IDs or trace IDs if available
- Link to related log queries or dashboards
- Default to Medium priority unless specified otherwise
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_19fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_9fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Draft Customer Reply<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_19fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_9fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Draft Customer Reply
Draft a reply to the customer about their issue.

## Guidelines
- Use the public product name only
- Avoid internal service names, codenames, or infrastructure details
- Don&#x27;t share internal error codes, file paths, or environment variables
- Stick to publicly documented features and standard troubleshooting steps

## When in doubt
Ask: &quot;Could a customer discover this through normal product usage?&quot;
If not, rephrase using general debugging approaches.
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_1dfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_dfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Search for Known Issues<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_1dfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_dfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Search for Known Issues
Search Slack to determine if an issue is already known.

## Workflow
1. Search with identifiers (ticket ID, error code, exact error message)
2. Narrow by channel and time range
3. Find threads with status, workaround, or owner info

## Output
- **Verdict:** Known / Possibly known / Not found
- **Best thread:** Permalink + summary
- **Next search:** Query to try if results are weak
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_1hfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_hfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Search Logs<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_1hfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_hfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Search Logs
Query Datadog logs for the specified request, user, or error.

## Common Patterns
- @requestId:{id} — find a specific request
- @userId:{id} or @email:{email} — find user activity
- status:error — filter to errors only
- service:{name} — filter by service

## Notes
- Always specify a time range (default: last 7 days)
- Field names vary by source—try multiple patterns
- Start broad, then narrow based on findings
</code></pre></div></div></div></div></div>
<h3 id="rules-and-skills-for-repeated-patterns" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#rules-and-skills-for-repeated-patterns" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Rules and Skills for repeated patterns</h3>
<p>We use Rules and Skills to automate common processes in support investigations.</p>
<div class="text-theme-text w-full " data-slot="accordion-root" data-orientation="vertical"><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_lldmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_5ldmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Customer reply (safe + actionable)<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_lldmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_5ldmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Skill: Customer reply (safe + actionable)

## Inputs I need
- Customer symptom (what they see)
- What we found (grounded summary)
- Next step/workaround (if any)
- 0–2 missing data points to request

## Output format
- Short acknowledgment
- What we found (no internal details)
- What to try next (numbered steps)
- If needed: two questions max (to unblock investigation)
- Close with what we&#x27;ll do next on our side

## Guardrails
- Avoid internal implementation details and internal jargon
- Prefer concrete steps over speculation
- Keep it concise; optimize for &quot;first useful reply&quot;
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_pldmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_9ldmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Draft a high-quality bug ticket<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_pldmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_9ldmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Skill: Draft a high-quality bug ticket

## Inputs I need
- Symptom (customer-visible)
- Time window
- Any IDs (request id, user/team id)
- Evidence snippets (sanitized)

## Output format
## Summary
## Expected vs Actual
## Steps to Reproduce
## Evidence
## Scope/Severity
## Suggested next debugging step

## Quality bar
- No vague language (&quot;sometimes&quot;, &quot;doesn&#x27;t work&quot;) without a concrete condition
- No internal-only jargon in the title
- Redact customer-specific info unless explicitly approved
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_tldmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_dldmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Known-issue researcher (Slack + Notion)<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_tldmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_dldmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Skill: Known-issue researcher (Slack + Notion)

## Inputs I need
- Exact error text (or best approximation)
- Feature area keywords
- Time window (default: last 30 days)

## Workflow
- Search Slack first for exact phrases and identifiers.
- If results are weak, broaden with feature keywords and time filters.
- Search Notion for runbooks/FAQs for the same feature area.

## Output format
- Verdict: Known / Possibly known / Not found
- Best thread(s): 1–3 links with a one-line &quot;why relevant&quot;
- Workaround / mitigation (if present)
- Next search refinement: exact query to run next
</code></pre></div></div></div></div></div>
<h3 id="subagents-to-run-steps-in-parallel" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#subagents-to-run-steps-in-parallel" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Subagents to run steps in parallel</h3>
<p>Subagents let us run common steps in the support process in parallel rather than sequentially.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>LogInvestigator</strong> searches Datadog for the failure point and supporting evidence.</li>
<li><strong>KnownIssueMiner</strong> scans Slack and Notion for prior threads and workarounds.</li>
<li><strong>TicketWriter</strong> formats the evidence into a complete escalation.</li>
<li><strong>CustomerReplyDrafter</strong> writes the customer response, stripping out internal details.</li>
</ul>
<p>The results merge into a single output that we review and send.</p>
<div class="text-theme-text w-full " data-slot="accordion-root" data-orientation="vertical"><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_5vdmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_1vdmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Here is a subagent config you can adapt. <h2 id="ai-native-technical-support" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#ai-native-technical-support" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>AI-native technical support</h2>
<p>By combining these tools, we bring code research directly into the technical support process. We estimate this allows our team to be as much as an order of magnitude more productive compared to traditional approaches, which require more jumping between tools and across teams. This productivity gain enables our small (but growing) team of support engineers to effectively support our rapidly scaling user base.</p>

">AI-native technical support</a></li></ul></div></div></nav><div class="prose prose--block prose--blog col-span-full!"><p>Support investigations are fundamentally research problems, which is why the slowest part of responding to customer challenges has always been gathering the right context. By collapsing code, logs, team knowledge, and past conversations into a single Cursor session, we&#x27;ve removed that bottleneck for most of our work.</p>
<p>Today, over 75% of Cursor&#x27;s support interactions run through Cursor itself, increasing support engineer throughput 5–10x. This has led to a step-change in what is possible for support engineers from just a year ago.</p>
<h2 id="starting-from-the-codebase" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#starting-from-the-codebase" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Starting from the codebase</h2>
<p>When we investigate, we typically begin in Ask Mode. We point it at the symptom and let it trace backward through the relevant product behavior. Because our full codebase is available locally, Cursor can index and use semantic search across product code, docs, and internal tooling in the same session.</p>
<p>This is where multi-root workspaces become powerful. Product context almost always spans multiple repositories. Answering the user question, &quot;Why is this button disabled?&quot; might involve frontend logic, backend policy checks, and docs describing the expected behavior. We keep related repositories together in one workspace so that kind of question is answerable in a single thread.</p>
<h2 id="integrating-support-sources-with-mcp" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#integrating-support-sources-with-mcp" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Integrating support sources with MCP</h2>
<p>We use MCP servers to retrieve context and bring it into our investigations. Our support engineers no longer need to search across several tools to retrieve pertinent context because it is available in Cursor.</p>
<p>MCP servers allow us to integrate:</p>
<ul>
<li>Databases with customer information, such as subscription tier, team settings, and privacy settings</li>
<li>Streamed event logs containing details on services used, telemetry errors, and network issues</li>
<li>Communication platforms like Slack, filled with threads and conversations that fill out our understanding of how customers interact with the product.</li>
<li>Engineering ticket platforms containing potentially dozens of unique teams that each operate differently</li>
<li>An internal documentation service that contains run books and troubleshooting guides</li>
<li>An account management service containing crucial customer information that may change the tone of how you approach a customer</li>
</ul>
<p>With Cursor and MCP servers, our support engineers can quickly pull necessary information directly into their codebase investigations.</p>
<h3 id="identifying-where-the-failure-occurred" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#identifying-where-the-failure-occurred" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Identifying where the failure occurred</h3>
<p>When a customer reports an error, we need to understand: Is the problem they&#x27;re experiencing reproducible or transient, and where exactly did Cursor fail (client-side, API edge, downstream dependency, auth). Datadog MCP lets us pull the relevant logs and traces directly into the investigation thread, allowing us to start narrowing down the possibilities.</p>
<h3 id="tracking-down-similar-cases" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#tracking-down-similar-cases" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Tracking down similar cases</h3>
<p>When a new support ticket comes in, the issue has likely been seen by another customer or someone on our team. An MCP that integrates with your support platform, as well as Slack, allows us to search that context directly and bring the most relevant threads back into the investigation. We search for hard identifiers first (error strings, request IDs), broaden if needed, and look for the newest thread that includes a current status, a workaround, and an owner.</p>
<h3 id="determining-whether-it-was-a-bug" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#determining-whether-it-was-a-bug" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Determining whether it was a bug</h3>
<p>A lot of investigations come down to &quot;bug or expected behavior?&quot; Notion MCP lets us pull the relevant runbook into the thread, cross-reference it against what we&#x27;re seeing, and either confirm the behavior or escalate with a much clearer bug report.</p>
<h3 id="filing-a-bug-report" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#filing-a-bug-report" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Filing a bug report</h3>
<p>By the time we finish an investigation in Cursor, we&#x27;ve gathered all the material we need to file a ticket with engineering if something needs to be fixed. The Linear MCP lets us take all of that context and turn it into a formatted escalation directly from the same thread.</p>
<h3 id="documentation-updates" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#documentation-updates" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Documentation updates</h3>
<p>When multiple customers run into the same questions, it&#x27;s often a sign that we need to improve our documentation. Technical support is well-positioned to implement these kinds of fixes directly. We just mention @Cursor in Slack with what needs updating, and a cloud agent will open a PR against our docs repo.</p>
<h2 id="automating-the-process" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#automating-the-process" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Automating the process</h2>
<h3 id="commands-for-common-steps" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#commands-for-common-steps" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Commands for common steps</h3>
<p>We use slash commands for the most frequently repeated steps in the process:</p>
<div class="text-theme-text w-full " data-slot="accordion-root" data-orientation="vertical"><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_15fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_5fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Create Support Ticket<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_15fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_5fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Create Support Ticket
Create a Linear ticket for the reported bug or user issue.

## Format
- **Reporter Information:** Email, account ID, platform, app version
- **Summary:** Brief 1-2 sentence description
- **Expected vs Actual:** What should happen vs what happens
- **Steps to Reproduce:** Numbered list

## Notes
- Gather user info from logs before creating the ticket
- Include request IDs or trace IDs if available
- Link to related log queries or dashboards
- Default to Medium priority unless specified otherwise
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_19fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_9fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Draft Customer Reply<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_19fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_9fdmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Draft Customer Reply
Draft a reply to the customer about their issue.

## Guidelines
- Use the public product name only
- Avoid internal service names, codenames, or infrastructure details
- Don&#x27;t share internal error codes, file paths, or environment variables
- Stick to publicly documented features and standard troubleshooting steps

## When in doubt
Ask: &quot;Could a customer discover this through normal product usage?&quot;
If not, rephrase using general debugging approaches.
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_1dfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_dfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Search for Known Issues<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_1dfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_dfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Search for Known Issues
Search Slack to determine if an issue is already known.

## Workflow
1. Search with identifiers (ticket ID, error code, exact error message)
2. Narrow by channel and time range
3. Find threads with status, workaround, or owner info

## Output
- **Verdict:** Known / Possibly known / Not found
- **Best thread:** Permalink + summary
- **Next search:** Query to try if results are weak
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_1hfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_hfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Search Logs<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_1hfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_hfdmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Search Logs
Query Datadog logs for the specified request, user, or error.

## Common Patterns
- @requestId:{id} — find a specific request
- @userId:{id} or @email:{email} — find user activity
- status:error — filter to errors only
- service:{name} — filter by service

## Notes
- Always specify a time range (default: last 7 days)
- Field names vary by source—try multiple patterns
- Start broad, then narrow based on findings
</code></pre></div></div></div></div></div>
<h3 id="rules-and-skills-for-repeated-patterns" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#rules-and-skills-for-repeated-patterns" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Rules and Skills for repeated patterns</h3>
<p>We use Rules and Skills to automate common processes in support investigations.</p>
<div class="text-theme-text w-full " data-slot="accordion-root" data-orientation="vertical"><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_lldmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_5ldmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Customer reply (safe + actionable)<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_lldmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_5ldmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Skill: Customer reply (safe + actionable)

## Inputs I need
- Customer symptom (what they see)
- What we found (grounded summary)
- Next step/workaround (if any)
- 0–2 missing data points to request

## Output format
- Short acknowledgment
- What we found (no internal details)
- What to try next (numbered steps)
- If needed: two questions max (to unblock investigation)
- Close with what we&#x27;ll do next on our side

## Guardrails
- Avoid internal implementation details and internal jargon
- Prefer concrete steps over speculation
- Keep it concise; optimize for &quot;first useful reply&quot;
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_pldmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_9ldmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Draft a high-quality bug ticket<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_pldmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_9ldmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Skill: Draft a high-quality bug ticket

## Inputs I need
- Symptom (customer-visible)
- Time window
- Any IDs (request id, user/team id)
- Evidence snippets (sanitized)

## Output format
## Summary
## Expected vs Actual
## Steps to Reproduce
## Evidence
## Scope/Severity
## Suggested next debugging step

## Quality bar
- No vague language (&quot;sometimes&quot;, &quot;doesn&#x27;t work&quot;) without a concrete condition
- No internal-only jargon in the title
- Redact customer-specific info unless explicitly approved
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" class="border-theme-border-02 border-t last:border-b focus-within:relative focus-within:z-1 " data-slot="accordion-item"><h3 data-orientation="vertical" data-state="closed" class="flex"><button type="button" aria-controls="radix-_R_tldmav5ubsl2ivb_" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed" data-orientation="vertical" id="radix-_R_dldmav5ubsl2ivb_" class="group pt-[0.98rem] pb-[1.05rem] flex flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-between text-left " data-slot="accordion-trigger" data-radix-collection-item="">Known-issue researcher (Slack + Notion)<span class="ml-g1 h-5 w-5"><span class="inline group-data-[state=open]:hidden"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></span><span class="hidden group-data-[state=open]:inline"><span class="icon-glyph-11" aria-hidden="true">↑</span></span></span></button></h3><div data-state="closed" id="radix-_R_tldmav5ubsl2ivb_" role="region" aria-labelledby="radix-_R_dldmav5ubsl2ivb_" data-orientation="vertical" class="overflow-hidden " data-slot="accordion-content" style="--radix-accordion-content-height:var(--radix-collapsible-content-height);--radix-accordion-content-width:var(--radix-collapsible-content-width)"><div class="pb-v1 text-theme-text"><div class="prose-code-block"><pre><code># Skill: Known-issue researcher (Slack + Notion)

## Inputs I need
- Exact error text (or best approximation)
- Feature area keywords
- Time window (default: last 30 days)

## Workflow
- Search Slack first for exact phrases and identifiers.
- If results are weak, broaden with feature keywords and time filters.
- Search Notion for runbooks/FAQs for the same feature area.

## Output format
- Verdict: Known / Possibly known / Not found
- Best thread(s): 1–3 links with a one-line &quot;why relevant&quot;
- Workaround / mitigation (if present)
- Next search refinement: exact query to run next
</code></pre></div></div></div></div></div>
<h3 id="subagents-to-run-steps-in-parallel" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#subagents-to-run-steps-in-parallel" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Subagents to run steps in parallel</h3>
<p>Subagents let us run common steps in the support process in parallel rather than sequentially.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>LogInvestigator</strong> searches Datadog for the failure point and supporting evidence.</li>
<li><strong>KnownIssueMiner</strong> scans Slack and Notion for prior threads and workarounds.</li>
<li><strong>TicketWriter</strong> formats the evidence into a complete escalation.</li>
<li><strong>CustomerReplyDrafter</strong> writes the customer response, stripping out internal details.</li>
</ul>
<p>The results merge into a single output that we review and send.</p>

<h2 id="ai-native-technical-support" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#ai-native-technical-support" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>AI-native technical support</h2>
<p>By combining these tools, we bring code research directly into the technical support process. We estimate this allows our team to be as much as an order of magnitude more productive compared to traditional approaches, which require more jumping between tools and across teams. This productivity gain enables our small (but growing) team of support engineers to effectively support our rapidly scaling user base.</p>
